what: Kaula conduct (kaulācāra), the five tattvas, the bhāvas and the āmnāya scheme in the eastern Kālī cult

evidence.detail: the Kālī tantras and Bengali digests cite the Kulārṇava and Kaulāvalīnirṇaya; the Kālīvilāsa and Kaulāvalī share the 'inwardly Śākta' verse

what: Dakṣiṇakālī's meditation and worship, the Mahāvidyā system

evidence.detail: Kṛṣṇānanda's Tantrasāra quotes the Kālī Tantra and the Muṇḍamālā

what: The Dakṣa–Satī myth, developed into the dismemberment of Satī's body and the pīṭhas

evidence.detail: the older Dakṣa-sacrifice narrative (epic, Purāṇas) is extended in the Kālikā Purāṇa with the scattering of the body

what: The yoginī cults and cremation-ground rites of the Yāmala tantras, domesticated and interiorised in the Kaula

evidence.detail: shared yoginī-kaula vocabulary; Kaulajñānanirṇaya's yoginī transmission

what: Matsyendra's Kaula teaching (yoginīkaula) as the root of the Nāth lineage

evidence.detail: the Kaulajñānanirṇaya is 'brought down by Macchaghnapāda' (colophons); the Nāths claim Matsyendra as their first human guru

what: The Kaula mode of Śrīvidyā worship and the Dakṣiṇāmnāya placement of Tripurasundarī

evidence.detail: the āmnāya scheme; the Kulārṇava's Ūrdhvāmnāya and Śrīprāsāda-parā mantra (ch. 3)

what: The goddess Tārā (with Ekajaṭā and Akṣobhya) and the 'Cīna' mode of her worship

evidence.detail: the Hindu Tārā texts themselves say Tārā's Kula worship was learned in Mahācīna from the Buddha (Rudrayāmala 17; Tārā Tantra 1.2-4)
Akṣobhya on Tārā's head in her meditation verse; Ekajaṭā as companion in both traditions

what: The self-decapitated goddess (Buddhist Chinnamuṇḍā-Vajrayoginī / Hindu Chinnamastā)

evidence.detail: iconographic parallel (severed head held in the hand, blood streams to two attendants); priority disputed

what: The four seats (Oḍḍiyāna, Jālandhara, Pūrṇagiri, Kāmarūpa) and pīṭha/upapīṭha lists shared with the Buddhist Yoginī tantras

evidence.detail: the same four seats in the Kubjikāmata (11.7), the Kālikā Purāṇa (18.41-43) and the Buddhist Hevajra/Cakrasaṃvara corpus
Śaiva/Śākta priority argued by some scholars; disputed

what: Kālī devotion, the Śyāmā songs and the tantric sādhanas taught by the Bhairavī Brāhmaṇī

evidence.detail: Ramakrishna's worship at Dakshineswar and his singing of Rāmprasād's songs (U52)

what: The Mālinī order of letters and Trika mantra material in the Kubjikāmata

evidence.detail: KMT chs. 4-5 on Mālinī (chapter titles in the GRETIL text)
